tasks.question: What might happen if we all switched to electric cars?

cues.cue: electric cars / cut / pollution
models: It could well be that electric cars cut pollution significantly, which would mean cleaner air in cities, and if so public health could improve noticeably.

cues.cue: electricity demand / rise / sharply
models: One possibility is that electricity demand would rise sharply, which might account for pressure on power grids, and therefore new infrastructure would be needed.

cues.cue: petrol stations / close / across the country
models: It is not impossible that petrol stations would close across the country, and this would help to explain the need for widespread charging networks.

cues.cue: car prices / fall / as production scales up
models: It may well be the case that car prices would fall as production scales up, particularly given how quickly battery costs are dropping, so electric cars would become more accessible.

cues.cue: traffic noise / drop / considerably
models: Perhaps traffic noise would drop considerably, and if that is true, then city life could feel noticeably calmer.

cues.cue: recycling systems / struggle / with old batteries
models: It is worth considering that recycling systems might struggle with old batteries, which raises the possibility that a new environmental issue could emerge, and so proper planning matters.

tasks.question: What could life be like if everyone worked from home?

cues.cue: everyone / work / from home
models: One possibility is that everyone will work from home, which might account for far less traffic during rush hour, and therefore cities could feel much quieter.

cues.cue: office buildings / stand / empty across cities
models: Conceivably, office buildings would stand empty across cities, and this cannot be ruled out, since many companies have already reduced their physical space.

cues.cue: local high streets / suffer / from less footfall
models: It could well be that local high streets would suffer from less footfall, which would mean small businesses losing customers, and if so town centres could decline further.

cues.cue: family life / benefit / from more flexible schedules
models: It may well be the case that family life would benefit from more flexible schedules, particularly given the extra time saved on commuting, so work-life balance could improve.

cues.cue: isolation / become / a growing concern for workers
models: It might be argued that isolation would become a growing concern for workers, though this remains open to question, because some people thrive with less social contact.

cues.cue: housing demand / shift / away from city centres
models: There could be a situation where housing demand shifts away from city centres, which would lead to smaller towns growing rapidly, and as a result property prices there could rise.

tasks.question: What might change if English stopped being the world's main language?

cues.cue: English / lose / its dominance
models: It might be argued that English would lose its dominance, though this remains open to question, because the language is deeply embedded in global business and science.

cues.cue: international business / adopt / a different common language
models: One possibility is that international business would adopt a different common language, which might account for major shifts in global trade patterns, and therefore new skills would become valuable.

cues.cue: translation technology / become / even more essential
models: It could well be that translation technology would become even more essential, which would mean less pressure to learn a single global language, and if so multilingualism would flourish.

cues.cue: education systems / adjust / their language curricula
models: Conceivably, education systems would adjust their language curricula, and this cannot be ruled out, since schools regularly respond to shifts in global demand.

cues.cue: several languages / share / global influence instead
models: It is not impossible that several languages would share global influence instead, and this would help to explain a more balanced linguistic landscape worldwide.

cues.cue: learning English / stay / valuable regardless
models: It is worth considering that learning English would stay valuable regardless, which raises the possibility that its role would shift rather than disappear entirely, and so complete decline seems unlikely.

tasks.question: What could happen if cities kept growing at this rate?

cues.cue: cities / become / too crowded
models: Conceivably, cities could become too crowded, and this cannot be ruled out, since population growth shows no sign of slowing.

cues.cue: housing prices / soar / beyond most people's reach
models: It could well be that housing prices would soar beyond most people's reach, which would mean many residents being pushed further from city centres, and if so commuting times would increase.

cues.cue: public services / struggle / to keep pace with demand
models: It may well be the case that public services would struggle to keep pace with demand, particularly given limited funding for expansion, so quality of life could suffer.

cues.cue: green spaces / disappear / to make way for housing
models: One possibility is that green spaces would disappear to make way for housing, which might account for a decline in residents' wellbeing, and therefore planning restrictions may tighten.

cues.cue: satellite towns / develop / around major cities
models: It is worth considering that satellite towns would develop around major cities, which raises the possibility that growth could be managed more sustainably, and so overcrowding might ease.

cues.cue: infrastructure / fail / to expand quickly enough
models: It might be argued that infrastructure would fail to expand quickly enough, though this remains open to question, because some cities have shown they can adapt rapidly when needed.

tasks.question: What might the effects be if schools had no exams?

cues.cue: exams / disappear / one day
models: It is not impossible that exams will disappear one day, and this would help to explain growing interest in continuous assessment as an alternative.

cues.cue: student stress levels / fall / significantly
models: It could well be that student stress levels would fall significantly, which would mean healthier learning environments overall, and if so wellbeing would improve across schools.

cues.cue: motivation / decline / without clear targets
models: It might be argued that motivation would decline without clear targets, though this remains open to question, because many students are driven by curiosity rather than grades alone.

cues.cue: teachers / rely / more on coursework and projects
models: One possibility is that teachers would rely more on coursework and projects, which might account for a more practical style of assessment, and therefore skills beyond memorisation would matter more.

cues.cue: universities / find / it harder to compare applicants
models: It may well be the case that universities would find it harder to compare applicants, particularly given the loss of a standard measure, so new admission methods would be needed.

cues.cue: creativity / flourish / without exam pressure
models: Perhaps creativity would flourish without exam pressure, and if that is true, then classrooms could become far more engaging places to learn.

tasks.question: What could happen if people spent less time online?

cues.cue: people / spend / less time online
models: It is worth considering that people might spend less time online, which raises the possibility that face-to-face relationships could strengthen, and so communities might feel closer again.

cues.cue: mental health / improve / for many users
models: It could well be that mental health would improve for many users, which would mean lower rates of anxiety linked to social comparison, and if so overall wellbeing would rise.

cues.cue: productivity / increase / with fewer digital distractions
models: It may well be the case that productivity would increase with fewer digital distractions, particularly given how much time is lost to notifications, so work quality could improve.

cues.cue: advertising industries / lose / significant revenue
models: One possibility is that advertising industries would lose significant revenue, which might account for major shifts in how companies reach customers, and therefore marketing strategies would need to change.

cues.cue: outdoor activities / become / more popular again
models: Conceivably, outdoor activities would become more popular again, and this cannot be ruled out, since many people already express a desire to spend less time on screens.

cues.cue: sleep quality / improve / for a large number of people
models: Perhaps sleep quality would improve for a large number of people, and if that is true, then overall health across the population could benefit.
